title: Adaptive Safety Throttle for Optimize Enactments
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Optimize suggestions (batching/caching profiles) can produce cost savings but may also change tail latency and error characteristics. We need a first-class enactor that applies suggestions automatically while protecting customer SLOs and allowing operators to pause/inspect. This ticket adds an adaptive safety throttle that controls adoption rate, ties into our canary simulation harness, and exposes operator checkpoints when metric thresholds are approached. Goals: (1) enable safe, incremental activation of Optimize recommendations with automatic rollback on regressions; (2) minimize manual triage while ensuring high-risk rollouts surface for human review; (3) provide clear observability and audit trail for every activation attempt.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive throttle can progressively ramp a new batching/caching profile from 0% -> 100% traffic with configurable step size and dwell time
Telemetry gates evaluate p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and inference token throughput at each ramp step and block progression when thresholds are exceeded
Automatic rollback triggers when predefined hysteresis conditions are met (e.g., sustained +10% p95 latency for 5 minutes)
Operator checkpoint is created at configurable milestones (25%, 50%, 75%) requiring ack for further ramp when 'operator_ack_required' is set
All activations produce an immutable audit record with suggested config, sampled request IDs, and link to simulation run
End-to-end e2e test in CI simulates canary traffic and asserts no regressions in golden metrics for a reference model/workload
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Dry-run in sandbox, collect baseline metrics via simulate-canary harness
Stage 1: 1% live ramp (15 minute dwell) with telemetry gating; no customer-affecting routing until pass
Stage 2: 10% ramp (30 minute dwell) with operator checkpoint if configured
Stage 3: 50% ramp with automated checks and optional manual review
Stage 4: 100% promotion or rollback based on gating outcomes and operator input
Fallback: immediate rollback and circuit-breaker for customers exceeding latency/error thresholds
canary_policy: Per-customer canary using adaptive token-bucket throttle. Ramp increments configurable per-customer class (free, standard, enterprise). Canary traffic includes a blend of synthetic probes and 1/N sampled real requests. Policy supports simulated canaries (offline) and live micro-canaries (1-10% traffic). Canary evaluation window and significance thresholds are parameterized. Built-in safety multiplier reduces step size automatically when variance in p95/p99 is high.
telemetry_gates: Gates examine a small set of golden metrics: p50 latency delta, p95 latency delta, p99 latency delta, request error-rate delta, model throughput, and cost-per-token estimate. Gates run on rolling windows (1m, 5m, 15m) and require both short and sustained checks. Gate thresholds are policy-driven (e.g., p95 delta > +10% sustained for 5m => block). A secondary gate monitors downstream customer-facing error codes and invokes immediate rollback if any increase beyond baseline is observed.
rollback_strategy: Three-tier rollback: (1) Automatic soft rollback: step back one ramp increment and re-evaluate; (2) Automatic hard rollback: revert to previous config and activate circuit-breaker for affected customers; (3) Manual rollback: operator-triggered revert with postmortem workflow. All rollbacks annotate the audit trail and trigger incident notifications to the on-call and product owners.
operator_workflow: Operators receive a notification at each configured checkpoint with: summary dashboard, top correlated queries, sample traces, and a suggested action (proceed/hold/rollback). Operator UI allows adding context notes and force-ack. If operator_ack_required is true and ack not received within timeout, system defaults to hold and not progress.
risks: False positives from noisy telemetry could block benign cost-saving changes
Insufficient sampling in low-traffic customers may hide regressions until after promotion
Operator overload if checkpoints are too frequent or thresholds too conservative
Rollback churn could oscillate configurations; need hysteresis and cooldowns
test_plan: Unit tests for throttle controller logic (step increments, dwell timers, backoff)
Integration test: link throttle to simulate-canary harness and assert gating semantics
Chaos test: induce synthetic latency spikes during ramp and assert automatic rollback
Canary validation CI: run against representative workloads and compare to golden baseline metrics
